If the files cannot be produced, mark both source entries IN PLACE as unverifiable rather than deleting them: retain array indices 2 and 3, set disposition to 'unverifiable_absent_from_repository_history', attach the absence evidence, and rewrite the GATE-AUTHORITY-PARITY-TOOL note so its basis no longer rests on the unverifiable document. options: HD-01-A locate and commit the files
HD-01-B delete the two sources and correct the counts
HD-01-C ratify with a standing exception, plan bytes unchanged

problem: MASTER-V2 source_plan_consolidation cites two documents with specific sha256 values that have never existed in any commit on any ref: EAFIX_REGISTRY_POST_MERGE_REMEDIATION_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v1_1_0.json and EAFIX_REGISTRY_POST_MERGE_REMEDIATION_PLAN_AMENDMENT_v1_0_1.json. Live plan logic (GATE-AUTHORITY-PARITY-TOOL) depends on the v1.1.0 semantics.
rationale: git log --all --diff-filter=ADMR across full history returns no match for either filename, so the files were never committed; they were almost certainly produced in a chat session and lost. Recovery (A) is cheap and fully preserves provenance, so it must be attempted first, but it is a search, not a decision. Between the fallbacks, HD-01-B is disproportionately costly: the obligation matrix carries 13 positional JSON pointers of the form /source_plan_consolidation/sources/N, one per source at indices 0 through 12. The two unverifiable sources sit at indices 2 and 3, so deleting them shifts indices 4 through 12 down by two and leaves pointers /sources/11 and /sources/12 dangling, corrupting 11 of 13 pointers and forcing an obligation matrix regeneration. HD-01-C preserves structure but leaves an unverifiable assertion standing inside the root authority document. HD-01-D achieves C's structural safety and B's honesty simultaneously: the array keeps its shape so every pointer resolves, while the record itself now states the truth. Both B and D change plan bytes and therefore require the verification spec target_plan.sha256 and byte_size to be updated in the same commit; under D that is a single mechanical edit.

problem: Five byte-identical copies of MASTER-V2 (all sha256 1fc42c13..., 471712 bytes) exist in the canonical docs root, and eleven superseded source plans sit alongside the active plan with no supersession metadata.
rationale: The verification specification's target_plan.filename already names the bare form, so selecting it produces zero downstream reference churn while any other choice requires a coordinated update of the spec binding. Deletion of the other four is lawful because their bytes are provably identical, and the plan requires re-verifying hash equality at the moment of deletion. For the archive destination, 99_archive_superseded_do_not_route/ is the governed archive: it carries archive_manifest.json and an explicit routing_policy of do_not_route_by_default, and it belongs to the numbered folder scheme. EAFIX_auth_docs/superseded/ holds four files but has no manifest and no routing policy, so it cannot enforce non-routing. problem: Two doc_authority.json files exist. The 00_ copy (24 entries, updated 2026-06-21) claims to be the sole authority and states the working copy was removed, but the root copy (5 entries, generated 2026-06-22) still exists and is dated one day later.
rationale: The two files are not competing duplicates and their schemas are not incompatible, contrary to the initial reading. Both use the same core entry fields (authority_level, classification, description); the 00_ schema is a strict superset adding relative_path, path_status, supersedes, and superseded_by. Entry overlap is exactly one document (the routing instructions), and the two files AGREE on it (both authority_level 1, canonical). The union is 28 entries with zero conflicts, so the merge is close to mechanical rather than high-effort. The files are functionally complementary: the root file carries policy (decision_rule precedence, control_files, subject_authorities) that the 00_ file has none of, while the 00_ file carries the document inventory that the root file has almost none of. Choosing either alone (A or B) discards a whole functional half. The 00_ location is preferred as canonical because it sits in the folder named for document control and because its schema is the superset that can absorb the other without loss.

compatibility_impact: vNext modules array populated to 34 with every field traced to a named registry field; SHARED_LIBS retained under a separate classification; CONFLICT::MODULE_UNIVERSE resolvable; module_catalog.json flagged for regeneration.
decision: Define the atomic module identity universe as the 34 records in module_registry.jsonl (module_id 50000000000000000001 through ...0034) and populate the vNext catalog from it with an explicit field-mapping record. Classify SHARED_LIBS (module_id 50000000000000000099) as a non-atomic cross-cutting bucket retained OUTSIDE the 34, not as a 35th module. module_catalog.json is stale and must be regenerated from the registry.
numbering_dependency: Assumes DEC-REG-008 through DEC-REG-014 (ingestion decisions) are appended first. If they are not, renumber this block to start at DEC-REG-008.
options: HD-04-A populate the vNext catalog from module_registry.jsonl
HD-04-B populate from an owner-supplied external source
HD-04-C retire the vNext catalog entirely
problem: Three sources disagree on the module universe: module_catalog.json holds 27, module_registry.jsonl holds 34, and Claude_gen_atomic_module_catalog_vNext.json declares 34 but carries an empty modules array. CONFLICT::MODULE_UNIVERSE in the conflict queue records the 27-versus-34 gap as open.
rationale: Set comparison dissolves the 27-versus-34 framing. The catalog's 27 ids are 26 atomic modules (...0001 through ...0026), all of which are present in the registry, plus one outlier ...0099 = SHARED_LIBS. The registry's 34 are ...0001 through ...0034, a clean superset of the catalog's atomic set with eight modules added (...0027 through ...0034). So the true comparison is 26 atomic plus one non-atomic bucket versus 34 atomic, not 27 versus 34. This is independently corroborated by CONFLICT::PROCESS_COVERAGE, which records that the process catalog models 26 of 34 modules, and by process_registry.jsonl holding exactly 26 records: the 26 are the original universe and eight were added later. SHARED_LIBS is excluded from the 34 because it is a different kind of entity, carrying layer=unassigned, empty scope_in and scope_out, and a purpose of owning cross-cutting shared libraries; folding it in would corrupt the atomic-module semantics that MASTER-V2 PHASE-06 ratifies. HD-04-C is rejected because the catalog schema carries enrichment fields the registry does not.

HD-05-A is minimal, reversible, preserves the audit trail intact, and is the only option compatible with the verification package. The absolute Windows paths are part of the historical record and are annotated, never edited.

compatibility_impact: No artifact changes now. Governs the final status transition.
decision: HD-06 cannot be pre-decided; it is the output of executing the plan. What is decided now is the RULE. Ratify only if all four conditions hold: every finding closed or waived with a rationale; all twelve validations pass; the verification spec target_plan hash binding matches the canonical plan bytes; and the supersession checklist passes all ten steps including a zero-hit dangling-reference scan. Ratify-with-exceptions requires each exception to name the finding, the rationale, and a review date. Withhold if any validation fails or the hash binding is broken.
numbering_dependency: Assumes DEC-REG-008 through DEC-REG-014 (ingestion decisions) are appended first. If they are not, renumber this block to start at DEC-REG-008.
options: HD-06-A ratify
HD-06-B ratify with scoped exceptions
HD-06-C withhold ratification
problem: HD-06 governs the transition of MASTER-V2 from proposed_pending_owner_ratification to ratified. Deciding it at the end, under completion pressure, risks a subjective call.
rationale: Pre-committing the criteria converts the final gate from a judgment call into a mechanical check, which is the same fail-closed discipline the registry system applies everywhere else. Two conditions are made non-waivable because waiving them would silently invalidate the verification apparatus itself: the target_plan hash binding, and the dangling-reference scan. Everything else is waivable with a recorded rationale and a review date. The honesty-audit ratio of E1/E2 closures to E3-only and E5-only closures must be reported before the decision, not after, so that a plan closed largely on authority assertion is visible as such at the moment of ratification.
